title: North Korea says Sondok launch tested a new air-defence missile, as Kim Yo Jong rejects talks
dek: State media says Wednesday's test proved a newly designed air-defence system and that a cruise missile unit practised a strike on a mock airport. Seoul had said the missiles may have been ballistic.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
North Korea said on Thursday that the missiles it fired off its east coast on Wednesday were a test of a newly designed air-defence missile system, and that a long-range strategic cruise missile unit had staged a strike drill the same day. The launch came hours after leader Kim Jong Un's sister said Pyongyang saw no need to talk to the United States while Washington accused it of the record theft of cryptocurrency from the exchange Binance.

The test was carried out by the Missile Administration and overseen by Kim Jong-sik, a member of the ruling party's Central Military Commission, the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported, according to Yonhap. KCNA said the firing "proved the technical specifications and reliability of the new material and intelligent multiple guided mode of the projectile", as well as the system's ability to identify and track targets. It said a cruise missile subunit in the east fired a long-range strategic cruise missile at a "virtual airport target".

South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) had said on Wednesday that multiple missiles were launched from the Sondok area of South Hamgyong province and flew less than 300 km, and left open the possibility that they included a close-range ballistic missile, Yonhap reported. Yonhap's report did not include a South Korean assessment of the North's claim. The South Korean military was "monitoring the North's various movements under a robust South Korea-U.S. combined defense posture", it said on Wednesday.

## A run of tests

Before the North's announcement, The Korea Times had reported that, if confirmed as ballistic, it would be the third such launch in about a week. Last Thursday, 29 October, the North fired nearly a dozen short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area, less than a week after Seoul proposed military talks on their tense border. North Korean state media said Pyongyang tested a cluster warhead for tactical ballistic missiles on Saturday, a test Seoul did not say it had detected. On Wednesday, Shin Jong-woo of the Korea Defense and Security Forum told The Korea Times the weapon appeared to be a version of the Hwasong-11 short-range ballistic missile; KCNA's description of an air-defence test does not match that assessment, and neither account has been independently confirmed.

The official KCNA news agency on Wednesday also released a photograph of a warship under construction at the Nampho shipyard, which it said was "incomparably huge" compared with the North's 5,000-tonne destroyers, AP reported. Kim has said he wants a 10,000-tonne guided-missile cruiser.

## The Binance dispute

The launch followed a second statement in two days from Kim Yo Jong, a senior ruling-party official, rejecting the FBI's finding that the North Korean hacking group it calls TraderTraitor stole about $6 billion in crypto assets from Binance in a breach that began late on 29 October, the largest such theft on record. She called the accusation "an extension of Washington's invariable hostile policy", AP reported.

"It is our clear stand that we have no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons," she said. "The choice for peace includes dialogue of course, but this is not surely equated with national interests for us." On Tuesday she had called the FBI announcement "a trite provocation".

The FBI has published hundreds of crypto addresses it links to the theft and asked exchanges and other businesses to block transactions involving them.

## Why it matters

US President Donald Trump has said he wants to restore ties with Kim, and analysts quoted by AP said Pyongyang is likely using weapons tests to press Washington for concessions. The launches came as votes were being counted in the US midterm elections, in which Trump's Republicans lost control of both houses of Congress. Relations between the two Koreas have also worsened since mine blasts at their border in September wounded three South Korean soldiers; Seoul says the North planted the mines, and Pyongyang denies it.

For India, the launches add to instability in a region that matters to its Act East policy and its partnerships with Japan and South Korea, while the Binance case shows how far state-linked hacking now reaches into global financial markets that Indian investors also use. The FBI has said the stolen assets will be laundered in stages, which means exchanges anywhere that receive them may be asked to freeze them.
